docs.title: Robotics Docs
docs.text:
This repository holds the operating and development documentation for the robotics platforms of the NewUU Engineering School. It is written for the people who actually switch the machines on: instructors running lab sessions, students working through the training plan, and developers writing code that runs on the robot.

Every procedure here is written as a procedure. Steps are numbered, button combinations are exact, and safety requirements are marked as such. Follow them in the order given.

The site is available in English and Russian — switch with the language selector in the header. Use the icon next to it to switch between the light and dark theme.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: • Unitree G1 EDU — humanoid robot, EDU (secondary development) version. Full operating manual, calibration procedure, SDK and network setup, maintenance and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Before you touch a robot
docs.text:
Read G1 Safety first. It is short, and it contains the one thing every operator must know before the robot is powered on: how to stop it.

The emergency stop for the G1 is L2+B. There is no physical emergency stop button on this delivery.

docs.title: How the documentation is organised
docs.text: Section Use it when Overview You need the hardware configuration and the scope of the manual Safety Before every session, and during instructor briefings Controls reference You need a button combination or the mode state machine Workspace preparation You are setting up the room before a session Standard operating procedures You are powering on, walking, gesturing, dancing or shutting down Working on the gantry The robot is suspended for development or calibration Mobile application You are using the phone app, OTA updates, navigation or demo teaching Calibration The robot falls repeatedly or drifts and a reboot does not fix it Development You are writing code, connecting over SSH or extending the hardware Maintenance You are cleaning, charging or storing the robot Troubleshooting Something is not behaving as documented Training plan You are teaching students or tracking their progress

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation is maintained in the open. If you find an error or want to add material, open an Issue or a Pull Request.

docs.title: Issue rules
docs.text:
1. Check that you are filing in the correct repository.
  2. If you are reporting an error, check that no equivalent Issue exists yet.
  3. Fill in the title and description precisely.
  4. Prefix the title with one of: [BUG], [PROPOSAL], [QUESTION].

docs.title: Pull request rules
docs.text:
1. For small changes — typos, formatting — a Pull Request is preferred over an Issue.
  2. Describe the problem and your proposed fix. Reference the Issue number where one exists.
  3. Before changing formatting, confirm that the change is needed.
  4. Follow the prevailing Markdown style of the repository.
  5. Documentation is written in English. Keep procedures imperative and unambiguous.

docs.title: Local deployment
docs.text:
Run the documentation locally in a Docker container:

git clone https://github.com/NewUU-engineering/robotics-docs
cd robotics-docs
docker pull squidfunk/mkdocs-material
docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 -v ${PWD}:/docs squidfunk/mkdocs-material

Or with a Python virtual environment:

python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocs-static-i18n[material]"
mkdocs serve

The site is then available at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Unitree G1 EDU — Overview
docs.text:
This is the operating manual for the Unitree G1 EDU humanoid robot as delivered to the NewUU Engineering School. It covers startup, motion control, calibration, the mobile application, SDK development, maintenance and troubleshooting.

Read the safety page first

The emergency stop is L2+B. There is no physical emergency stop button on this delivery. Read Safety before powering the robot on, and brief every new operator on it.

docs.title: Firmware scope
docs.text:
This manual documents firmware V1.0.4. Check your firmware version in the mobile application under About before the first session.

Firmware earlier than V1.0.4

Firmware versions before V1.0.4 use L1 where V1.0.4 uses L2: Zero Torque is L1+B, Damping is L1+A, Lock Stand is L1+↑. Every combination in this manual assumes V1.0.4.

docs.title: Source precedence
docs.text:
When sources disagree, use them in this order:

  1. The legend printed on the remote control itself. Unitree's documentation directs operators to this legend as the primary reference.
  2. Official Unitree documentation for your firmware version.
  3. This manual.
  4. Your supplier, for anything the first three do not settle.

docs.title: Delivered hardware configuration
docs.text:
Component Specification Model Unitree G1, EDU version (secondary development) Configuration U2 — 3 DoF waist, 7 DoF arms PC1 Control board. Runs locomotion, stabilisation, and the links to the remote control and the mobile application. Not user-accessible PC2 NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 100 TOPS, Ubuntu 20.04 factory image. Fully available for your code PC1 ↔ PC2 Ethernet cable inside the robot Head Intel RealSense D435i depth camera and Livox MID-360 LiDAR (360° horizontal, 59° vertical). The LiDAR cable detaches from the board; the head is removed with a Torx driver, not a hex key Ports 4× USB Type-C (one carries DisplayPort), battery power output, pin header for boards such as a Raspberry Pi, 2× RJ45 Battery Indicator segments of 25% each. 5 V charger. Not interchangeable with the Go2 battery Spirit level Fitted on the back of newer batches. Used to level the robot during calibration Gantry Stand with a winch and sling. The robot can walk while suspended Calibration braces Mechanical stops for waist/torso, legs and feet, plus a camera brace. The Go2 set is separate Included tools T-handle driver and pliers Remote controls Two units in the case — one for the G1 and one for the Go2, labelled. All button combinations are printed on the remote Emergency stop button Not fitted. The distributor adds it only to turnkey solutions for the EU and US markets

Batch differences

Delivery batches differ. Newer units have a quieter and more stable head, a voice output at roughly half the volume, Wi-Fi enabled on the Jetson out of the box, a spirit level for calibration, and a different Jetson board and GPIO revision. Verify the configuration of your own unit rather than relying on a general description.

Certification

Robots in this delivery do not carry European certification as delivered. The large red button on top is fitted by the distributor only for turnkey products sold into the EU and US markets.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
New operators should work through the manual in this order:

  1. Safety — how to stop the robot, and the full safety checklist.
  2. Controls reference — the mode state machine and the complete button table.
  3. Workspace preparation — environment requirements and the pre-session checklist.
  4. Standard operating procedures — power-on through shutdown.
  5. Working on the gantry — the safe working position for everything else.

Developers continue with Development. Instructors should also read Calibration and Training plan.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: Calibration is the most demanding procedure in this manual. Read it end to end before starting.

docs.title: When to calibrate
docs.text:
Do not calibrate on a schedule

From the Unitree user manual: "G1 has been calibrated by default after leaving the factory. Do not recalibrate the joints for normal use! If any abnormal situation occurs with the G1, please consult Unitree's official technical support before determining whether joint recalibration is necessary."

Calibrate on symptoms, not on the calendar. A routine calibration performed without cause is a regular opportunity to break a working setup.

Calibrate when:

  • The robot falls frequently while walking and a reboot does not help.
  • The robot drifts consistently to one side when walking straight. Try remote drift compensation first — R1 + arrows.
  • The robot has taken a serious fall or impact.

Agree the calibration with your supplier before starting. The path in the application is Settings → Data → Robot → Calibration.

docs.title: The three levels of calibration
docs.text: Level Function Offset configuration Point adjustment of a specific motor's offset by numeric value. Includes a reset IMU calibration / raw pitch Balance adjustment — the robot's forward and backward lean, comparable to setting an artificial horizon Full body calibration Full calibration of every joint, either assisted (recommended) or manual

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
Step Action 1 Put the robot into Damping, then power it off completely 2 Remove the protective body covers if your version has them. Newer versions do not require this 3 Fit the mechanical braces on every joint: waist/torso, legs and feet 4 Tighten the brace screws. When tightening several screws on one part, tighten them evenly so the part is not skewed 5 Fit the camera brace 6 Lock the camera in the application 7 Level the robot, using the built-in spirit level on the back or the indicator in the application 8 Connect the charging cable. Calibrating on mains power is normal

Check the brace on the foot

The foot brace is the least visible of the braces and the one most often forgotten. A missing foot brace makes the calibration fail.

Torso brace deactivates the torso motors

With the torso brace fitted the robot walks but does not dance.

Do not overtighten long bolts

Leverage strips the bolt head. Broken bolts are a recurring failure, including in the hands of Unitree's own engineers.

docs.title: Full body calibration (assisted)
docs.text:
Step Action Expected result 1 Application → Full body calibration → Next The Development mode screen opens 2 Choose Assisted calibration, not Manual The robot starts its sweep 3 The robot drives most of the joints through their range by itself — 4 Legs: raise the leg fully up, then pull it towards you to the opposite stop. Repeat on the second leg Every joint reaches its mechanical stop 5 Feet: rotate the foot to its stop. In its final position the foot must be perfectly level This is the step most often skipped 6 Arms: drive the shoulder, elbow/forearm and wrist to their extreme positions The wrist ends fully rotated 7 Press Calibration / Next and step away from the robot — 8 Wait for the status calibration successful — 9 Reboot the robot — 10 Remove every brace — 11 Power the robot off and on once more The torso is controllable again

Step 11 is mandatory

Without the second power cycle after removing the braces, the torso motors stay deactivated.

The rule that governs calibration

Every joint must be driven to its full mechanical stop.

Assisted mode does not drive every joint automatically — some must be driven by hand. It is still far simpler than manual calibration.

docs.title: Success criteria
docs.text:
After the reboot, switch to a working mode and confirm all of the following:

  • The robot rises into its working stance by itself, with no manual help.
  • It stands centred and level, without trembling.
  • Its feet do not catch the floor.
  • Rocked forward and backward, it does not fall — it balances itself.
  • Walking straight, it does not drift sideways.
  • The application shows no flashing red indicator.

docs.title: Known failure mode
docs.text:
Stage Detail Symptom After calibration: a flashing red indicator and the error Communication, joint over limit Cause A brace was left on the foot. Assisted mode could not drive that joint to its stop, so the left and right legs ended up with different zero points Fix Free and level the feet, then repeat the full body calibration from the start Result The calibration succeeds and the robot is measurably more stable

Two hypotheses commonly raised for this symptom are wrong and waste time: the order of operations around Lock Stand, and a low battery charge. Check the braces first, starting with the feet.

docs.title: Controls reference
docs.text: All combinations on this page are for firmware V1.0.4. Verify your firmware in the mobile application under About before the first session.

docs.title: Mode state machine
docs.text:
POWER OFF
        │  battery button: one short press, then hold ≥2 s
        │  wait ~1 minute
        ▼
   ZERO TORQUE ─────────── joints are free, the robot is limp
        │                  reachable from any state: L2+Y
        │  L2+B
        ▼
   DAMPING ─────────────── motors are de-energised. A standing robot FALLS
        │  TTS: "Damp mode."  Do not move the joints by hand in this mode
        │                     This is also the EMERGENCY STOP
        │  L2+↑  (Lock Stand)
        ▼
   READY ───────────────── the pose is held, there is no active balancing
        │  TTS: "Ready mode."
        │  R2+A  (Run Control)   or   R1+Y  (Main Operation, 3-DoF waist)
        ▼                             R1+X  (for a 1-DoF waist)
   MOTION ──────────────── active balancing, stick control
        │  TTS: "Walk-around mode activated. Control your speed and stay alert."
        │  left stick — forward/backward · right stick — turn
        │
        ├──► START ─────────── toggle stand ⇄ walk
        ├──► 2×L2 / 2×L1 ───── low / high speed        (in R1+X, R1+Y)
        ├──► R2+↓ / R2+↑ ───── slow / fast run         (in R2+A)
        ├──► R1+arrows ─────── drift compensation      (in R1+X, R1+Y)
        ├──► 2×START ───────── continuous walking — not recommended
        └──► DANCE mode ────── hold the triangle button
                  └─ after the dance → automatically Run mode

   POSTURES (holding L2):
      L2+A → Squat Switch        L2+← → Seated Mode
      L2+X → Lying / Standing    L2+R2 → Debug Mode

   STOPPING LADDER (soft to hard):
      1× START  → stops walking, keeps standing        ← normal stop
      2× START  → interrupts a running action          ← cancel an animation
      L2+B      → Damping, sinks slowly to the floor   ← EMERGENCY
      battery   → only if the robot is suspended or seated  ← last resort

docs.title: Button combinations
docs.text:
Action Combination Power on / off Battery button: one short press, then hold ≥2 s Boot time ~1 minute to Zero Torque Zero Torque L2+Y Damping L2+B — from an active state, hold the combination rather than tapping it Lock Stand → Ready L2+↑ Squat Switch L2+A (toggle) Seated Mode L2+← Lying / Standing L2+X Debug Mode L2+R2 — enter while the robot is suspended and in Damping Run Control R2+A Main Operation Control (1-DoF waist) R1+X Main Operation Control (3-DoF waist — our robot) R1+Y — "Only Used For 3-DOF Waist Structure" Stand ⇄ walk single press of START Continuous walking double press of START — not recommended Low / high speed 2×L2 / 2×L1 (inside R1+X, R1+Y) Slow / fast run R2+↓ / R2+↑ (inside R2+A) Lean forward / backward hold START+↑ / START+↓ Drift compensation R1 + arrows (inside R1+X, R1+Y) Handshake SELECT+A (hold SELECT, press A) Wave hand SELECT+Y Turn around and wave SELECT+X Emergency stop L2+B — the robot sinks slowly to the floor Stand up from the floor L2+X Dance mode hold the triangle button; start a dance with R1+B Remote control calibration F1+F3 → rotate both sticks fully around → F3 to save

Remote control symbols

A triangle next to a button means hold it. A star means a short press.

docs.title: Motion modes
docs.text:
Mode Entry Character Main Operation Control R1+Y for our robot (3-DoF waist); R1+X for a 1-DoF configuration More stable, more assured, noticeably louder Run Control R2+A Faster, less stable gait

Unitree specifies R1+Y for robots with a 3-DoF waist: "Only Used For 3-DOF Waist Structure". Our unit has a 3-DoF waist, so R1+Y is the mode to use.

Continuous walking

A double press of START enables Continuous Walking, which Unitree marks as not recommended. Do not confuse it with the single press of START, which stops walking.

docs.title: Automatic power-off
docs.text: The robot powers itself off after 10 minutes of remote control inactivity.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
[Developer laptop]  192.168.123.200–250  (static — there is NO DHCP)
            │ Ethernet via the RJ45 on the back panel — the recommended route
            ▼
   ┌────────────────────────┐  Ethernet  ┌──────────────────────────┐
   │  PC2 = Jetson Orin NX  │◄──────────►│  PC1 = control board     │
   │  192.168.123.164       │ (internal) │  192.168.123.161         │
   │  100 TOPS, Ubuntu 20.04│            │  locomotion, balancing   │
   │  ← YOUR CODE RUNS HERE │            │  remote control, app     │
   │  ssh unitree / 123     │            │  DO NOT TOUCH            │
   └────────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────────┘
            │                                        ▲
            │ Livox MID-360 LiDAR                    │ direct radio link
            │ 192.168.123.20                   [remote control]
            ▼
   subnet mask for all hosts: 255.255.255.0

The split is a safety feature: if you crash PC2, PC1 keeps running. Locomotion and stabilisation are unaffected, because you never work on PC1 directly.

docs.title: Network setup
docs.text:
Device IP PC1 — control computer (locomotion) 192.168.123.161 PC2 — Jetson Orin NX (yours) 192.168.123.164 Livox MID-360 LiDAR 192.168.123.20 Your laptop 192.168.123.200–.250 Subnet mask 255.255.255.0

There is no DHCP server on the robot's network

Every address is assigned manually. Pick a free address in the 192.168.123.x subnet, in the range .200–.250.

docs.title: Over Ethernet — recommended
docs.text:
1. Run a cable between your laptop and the RJ45 on the robot's back panel.
  2. Network settings → Wired connection → Manual IPv4 → address 192.168.123.250, mask 255.255.255.0.
  3. Connect: ssh unitree@192.168.123.164, password 123.
  4. Confirm the fingerprint on the first connection.

docs.title: Over Wi-Fi
docs.text:
• On older batches, Wi-Fi on the Jetson is not activated. Enable it with sudo rfkill unblock all.
  • A static IP on the Wi-Fi hotspot removes internet access on the Jetson. Use Ethernet for development.

Additional hardware — a second Jetson, a Raspberry Pi and similar — connects through the free RJ45 and joins the same local network as PC1 and PC2.

Never change the wired network settings inside the robot

Recovering from a change here means opening the back panel and reinstalling the operating system. The interfaces you will see and must leave alone are: Ethernet, the Docker bridge, the bridged LAN and Wi-Fi, and the peer-to-peer LAN.

docs.title: SDK
docs.text:
Features land in C++ first, then Python, then ROS2. The ROS2 lag reaches a year.

Option When to choose it unitree_sdk2 (C++) Locomotion control and access to the newest features. The main repository, open source on GitHub, forkable. Pre-installed on the Jetson Python Starting point, integrations, speech. Installed with pip install ROS2 (Cyclone DDS) Navigation, SLAM, mapping, and attaching third-party modules

Use a Python virtual environment. Working outside one causes dependency conflicts and breaks on OS upgrades.

Operating system: Ubuntu 20.04 (the Jetson factory image) or 22.04. The SDK has also been adapted to Fedora Workstation; request that procedure from your supplier.

Why ROS2 over ROS1 here: ROS2 shares memory between nodes on different machines. Visualisation runs on the laptop while computation runs on the Jetson, inside a single parameter space. Third-party arms attach as a "second robot" in the same ecosystem.

docs.title: Develop mode
docs.text:
Once the G1 is powered on, the built-in motion control program starts automatically, even with no input from the remote control. It periodically sends instructions at speed 0. Using the SDK for low-level development in that state causes instruction conflicts, and the robot jitters.

This is also why the robot feels tense in Zero Torque: the built-in program is always running.

Enter Develop mode before any low-level development

Skipping this step produces command conflicts and makes the robot shake. Develop mode is available on the EDU version.

Step Action Check 1 Suspend the robot on the gantry and put it into Damping — 2 Press L2+R2 Develop mode is entered; the built-in program stops 3 Press L2+A The robot takes a specific diagnostic pose (position mode), confirming Develop mode is active 4 If the pose is wrong, press L2+R2 again until it is correct — 5 Press L2+B Back to Damping. You can now work with the SDK

docs.title: High level and low level
docs.text:
Level What it is Risk High level Unitree's built-in functions — stand, squat, walk, gestures Safe Low level Direct joint control across three domains: full body, legs, upper body You can physically break the robot if a joint is not in a valid position. Follow the procedure exactly

Locomotion client: squat, stand up, move(X, Y, Z) — X forward, Y sideways, Z rotation. Motion is two-dimensional; the robot does not walk upward.

One motor is three motors. What looks like a single motor from the outside contains three motors internally.

Where your code runs: on PC2 (the Jetson). Connecting directly to PC1 is technically possible and is not supported.

docs.title: Microphone audio
docs.text:
The SDK does not expose a realtime microphone stream. Audio is synchronised over multicast from PC1 to PC2, one way only.

  • Request the multicast group address and port from your supplier.
  • Resample the stream to 16 kHz for most ASR and LLM APIs.

docs.title: Simulators and motion learning
docs.text:
Tool Status Isaac Lab Recommended for reinforcement learning and imitation learning Gazebo Integration exists and is community-maintained, not official MuJoCo An alternative, weaker for these simulations

Stairs do not work out of the box

Climbing stairs requires retraining locomotion from scratch. The stated maximum step height is about 15 cm. Teams that have achieved stair climbing rewrote the locomotion stack completely.

docs.title: AI integration
docs.text:
Use a two-layer architecture:

   [Planner agent]  ──►  breaks the task into steps
   (reasoning model)     and calls the robot's functions
                                  │
                                  ▼
   [VLA — Visual Language Action]  ──►  executes the actions

Do not give a conversational live model direct joint control

A live conversational model is not reliable enough to control a robot and it makes mistakes. Live APIs are for dialogue, not for control.

  • Function calling: the model calls predefined robot functions. This requires correct context and prompting.
  • Reference integration: Google Gemini connected by API key, running locally from a laptop with the robot on Wi-Fi. Fast response comes from pre-generation — the model starts generating before the speaker finishes.
  • Unitree's world model for household tasks is under development and not yet available.

docs.title: Hardware extension
docs.text:
• Third-party hands such as the Inspire Robotics hand install plug and play: mount them, route the wiring correctly, and connect them to PC2.
  • Only the U2 configuration (7 DoF arms) supports external hands. The U1 configuration (5 DoF) has a restricted SDK and does not support these modifications. Our unit is U2.
  • Over ROS2 an additional module appears as a "second robot" and is controlled in the same loop.
  • The head can be modified: print a front panel on a 3D printer and turn the camera forward — it points downward as standard — or add a second camera.

Do not flash the Jetson Orin NX with third-party images

docs.title: Working on the gantry
docs.text: The gantry is the safe working position for development, calibration and diagnostics. Use it whenever the robot does not need to be walking on the floor.

docs.title: Mounting the robot
docs.text:
Step Action 1 Check which way round the mount is fitted. Mounted the wrong way round, it physically prevents the robot from moving 2 Raise the robot until the sling is slightly taut with the robot in its standing position 3 Do not lower the robot too far and do not raise it too high. Both are hazardous and neither is prevented in software 4 Close the sling catches on the gantry 5 Work in pairs: one person steadies and moves the stand, the other operates the remote

Suspended too high

A robot suspended too high and then powered on cannot feel the floor, cannot reach its working stance, and starts extending its legs erratically trying to reach the ground. Keep a finger on L2+B (Damping). If that does not settle it, power the robot off. This situation is uncommon but likely when working with students.

docs.title: Powering on a suspended robot
docs.text:
Step Action TTS 1 Apply power and wait ~1 minute — 2 The robot enters Zero Torque automatically — 3 Press L2+B Damp mode. 4 Run Lock Stand (L2+↑) Ready mode. 5 Only now may the robot be lowered or placed on the floor — 6 Switch to a working mode (R2+A or R1+Y) Walk-around mode activated…

Do not handle the robot before Lock Stand

Do not pick the robot up or manipulate its legs before the Lock Stand step. It will go limp and fall.

docs.title: Debug mode
docs.text: Debug Mode is L2+R2. Enter it while the robot is suspended and in Damping. Return to Damping with L2+B.

docs.title: Standby during development
docs.text: Leave the robot suspended on the gantry, connect the power cable — the indicator turns blue — and switch it to Zero Torque. In this state it does not stand under tension and is available for work at any moment.

docs.title: Removing the robot from the gantry
docs.text:
1. Pull the robot back slightly.
  2. Lift it by hand and clear it from the sling.
  3. Remove the catches.

docs.title: Why L2+B must be held
docs.text:
The asymmetry is deliberate:

  • When powering on, L2+B responds to a single short press.
  • When shutting down, or from an active state, a single press is not enough — the combination must be held.

This prevents an accidental brush against L2+B during operation from de-energising the motors and dropping a standing robot.

docs.title: LiDAR and optics
docs.text:
Never touch the LiDAR surface with your fingers

  • Clean with microfibre only, in a single light pass, without pressure.
  • A scratch on the protective dome deflects the laser and corrupts the LiDAR readings.
  • The LiDAR sees through the plastic dome. Contamination degrades its data, so remove the dome to clean it.

docs.title: Batteries
docs.text:
• Each indicator segment is 25% of charge.
  • Runtime is about 2 hours of continuous operation. A full day requires a second battery.
  • G1 and Go2 batteries are not interchangeable, and different G1 battery variants require different chargers. Do not substitute something that looks similar.
  • The charger runs at 5 V and connects to any power source or computer.

docs.title: Storage and idle periods
docs.text:
• Idle during the day: suspend the robot on the frame and switch it to Damping. Otherwise it falls when the battery runs out.
  • Long-term storage: remove the battery from the robot.
  • For development, keep the robot suspended on the gantry with the power cable connected.

docs.title: Lifting and shutdown
docs.text:
Keep your hands off the joints

Do not place your hands on the hip or knee joints when lifting the robot. They pinch.

Power off only when the robot is supported

Power the robot off only when it is suspended on the frame or seated on a chair, and in Damping. A standing robot with no support falls flat and can be damaged.

Forced shutdown — remote control dead, robot unresponsive: suspend the robot on the frame with its feet off the ground and at least 2 m of clear space, then press the battery button short, then long.

After shutdown, fit the arm and foot joint stops as required for storage so that the next startup runs correctly.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• The head is removed with a Torx driver, not a hex key.
  • The case includes a T-handle driver and pliers. Buy hex keys separately — the supplied ones are poor.
  • Do not lose the small calibration braces. They are easy to misplace, and calibration is impossible without them. Keep them in the case.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text: Step Action 1 Power the robot on and wait for it to boot 2 The robot raises a Wi-Fi access point (AP mode). This is the default and the recommended mode 3 Connect the phone to that access point 4 Open the application and press Start

docs.title: AP mode and Wi-Fi mode
docs.text:
Mode When to use it AP mode — the robot is the access point The default, and correct for nearly all work Wi-Fi mode — the robot joins an external network Firmware updates (OTA) and remote diagnostics by a support engineer

Warning

Firmware updates are unavailable in AP mode. Switch to Wi-Fi mode to update.

docs.title: Android connection issue
docs.text:
Symptom: the connection is stable on iOS, while on Android the robot periodically fails to connect.

Cause: many Android devices enable priority mode, which switches the system to mobile data when the Wi-Fi signal is weak and drops the link to the robot's access point.

Fix:

  1. Disable automatic switching to mobile data in the network settings.
  2. Or switch mobile data off for the duration of the session.
  3. On devices where that setting is unavailable — this occurs on some Samsung models — use a different phone.

Keep the application installed on several phones. Three, including a spare Android device, is a workable arrangement.

docs.title: Application sections
docs.text:
Section Function Body Info Communication quality (%), location of body parts, temperature and air cooling Calibration Full body calibration (assisted and manual), offset configuration, IMU calibration, slow reach. See Calibration Peripheral Remote control charge, rebinding a new remote, individual button tests, audio functions Update / Service Log retrieval and log upload, alarm information, service status, OTA box Security Internet remote connection — see the warning below About Serial number, software and hardware versions, firmware update, feedback Guide Video tutorials and the user manual. Covers startup and shutdown, posture and movement, debug mode, both calibration types, network connection, remote control timing, navigation. The manual is in English; request the Russian version from your supplier Motion marketplace Downloadable community motions and dances, including a side flip. Do not run advanced motions such as the side flip on an untested robot Demo teaching Kinaesthetic gesture teaching — see below Navigation LiDAR mapping and patrolling — see below Audio / AI Voice Wake-up conversation mode and the Doubao assistant — see below Locks Separate switches to lock the camera and the torso. Both are needed during calibration Settings Interface language, including Uzbek, and the 3D room view

Camera: the application takes photos and video. Video is capped at 30 seconds with an automatic stop — there is no need to press stop.

Internet remote connection

With this feature enabled, anyone signed in under the same account can connect to the robot from an external network and control it after you leave the local session. Enable it only deliberately and with a clear reason.

docs.title: Firmware updates (OTA)
docs.text:
1. Enable the OTA box in the Services section in advance. Without it, no update notifications arrive.
  2. Wait for the new-firmware notification. Unitree releases updates roughly every 2–3 months.
  3. Switch the robot to Wi-Fi mode. Updates are blocked in AP mode.
  4. Start the update from the About section.

docs.title: Demo Teaching
docs.text:
Step Action 1 Open Demo teaching → Create teaching 2 Press Start teaching 3 Guide the robot physically through the movement by hand 4 Press Stop → Save and give the gesture a name

Scope: teaching covers the upper body only — torso and arms. The legs do not participate.

Warning

Holding the robot unevenly during teaching skews the torso. Move the limbs smoothly and symmetrically.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Step Action 1 Put the robot into running or regular mode 2 Open Navigation and create a map, giving it a name 3 Walk the robot through the space. The LiDAR builds a 3D scan 4 Press Mark patrol point to mark a route point 5 Press Executable task to assign an action at that point — photo or video 6 Repeat for the remaining points and connect the points into a route 7 Press Save and start the route

On encountering an obstacle the robot announces There are obstacles in your way. Please be careful. and stops. Plan on the robot stopping: clear the route before running a patrol.

Check which map is open

Maps from different robots sit side by side in the application. A map recorded by a Go2 quadruped looks much like a G1 map in the list. Confirm which robot a map belongs to before using it.

docs.title: Doubao voice assistant
docs.text:
Wi-Fi is required. The assistant supports English and Chinese.

Step Action 1 Open Audio and enable Wake up conversation mode 2 Say the wake word followed by a command, for example "Hello robot", "Go forward" 3 The assistant replies, executes commands and plays music

Billing: this is a paid service. The starting balance is from $15, topped up through the Unitree website by the customer.

Alternative: connect your own LLM through an API key. See AI integration.

docs.title: Logs and diagnostics
docs.text:
Errors appear in red in the application. To send them to support:

  1. Run Log retrieval.
  2. Run Log upload.

Logs are not stored on the phone — they go straight to the Unitree cloud, where engineers analyse them.

docs.title: Standard operating procedures
docs.text: Every procedure on this page assumes firmware V1.0.4 and a workspace prepared according to Workspace preparation.

docs.title: Power-on sequence
docs.text:
Precondition: the battery is fitted, the space around the robot is clear, and the robot is lying down or standing with support.

Starting from lying or squatting

Start the robot from a lying or squatting position only on a flat, hard floor. With dexterous hands fitted, starting from lying or squatting is prohibited.

Step Action Result 1 Press the battery button once, briefly The indicator lights up 2 Press the same button again and hold for ≥2 seconds Boot starts 3 Wait ~1 minute. Do not touch the robot — 4 The robot enters Zero Torque mode automatically Joints are free, the arms hang loose 5 Press L2+B TTS: Damp mode. — the robot is in Damping 6 Press L2+↑ (Lock Stand) TTS: Ready mode. — the pose is locked 7 Press R2+A, or R1+Y for our 3-DoF configuration TTS: Walk-around mode activated… — the robot is ready to move

Do not move the joints by hand in Damping mode

Moving the joints manually while the robot is in Damping raises an error.

Do not run step 7 until the robot is stable

Move to the working mode only once the robot stands steadily or is suspended. Ready mode holds the pose but does not balance actively.

docs.title: Standing up from the floor
docs.text:
Precondition: the robot is lying down, in Zero Torque or Damping.

Danger

Stand the robot up only on a flat, hard floor. With dexterous hands fitted, standing up from lying is prohibited.

Both starting positions work: the robot lying flat on its back in a correct pose, and the robot lying in an arbitrary, tangled pose.

Step Action 1 Confirm that nobody is within arm's reach 2 Press L2+X — Lying and Standing switches between the lying and standing positions 3 TTS: Robot rising. Please stand clear. — step back 4 TTS: Walk-around mode activated. Control your speed and stay alert.

docs.title: Walking
docs.text:
The remote control is highly sensitive

Move the sticks smoothly, in small increments.

Control Function Left stick Walk forward / backward Right stick Turn left / right START Toggle stand ⇄ walk 2×L2 / 2×L1 Low / high speed (inside R1+X, R1+Y) R2+↓ / R2+↑ Slow / fast run (inside R2+A) Hold START+↑ / START+↓ Lean the body forward / backward R1 + arrows Drift compensation — see Troubleshooting

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Walking backwards is unstable and the robot can fall. This is a limitation of the current locomotion algorithm, not a fault of the unit. Walk backwards only with a spotter or on the gantry.
  • The robot withstands a light push from the side. It compensates and stays upright.
  • If the robot starts drifting sideways, correct it with the forward stick — it will recover balance. Systematic drift calls for drift compensation, and if that does not resolve it, calibration.

docs.title: Why the gait looks unusual
docs.text: Earlier locomotion training used a "virtual point" that pulled the robot forward, and the robot pushed back against it. The current version adds the model's weight in simulation and pushes it instead. The gait is more natural as a result, but the robot sits down slightly when moving backwards as it works to stay upright.

docs.title: Interactive gestures
docs.text:
Precondition: the robot is standing in a working mode.

Step Action 1 Turn the robot to face the person, using the right stick 2 Hold SELECT and press the gesture button 3 The robot performs the gesture 4 Press the same combination again — the arm returns to its starting position Gesture Combination Handshake SELECT + A Wave hand SELECT + Y Turn around and wave SELECT + X

Gestures do not affect balance. The robot keeps standing steadily throughout.

docs.title: Dance mode
docs.text:
The most hazardous of the basic demonstrations

The robot makes wide, sweeping movements and can strike a person.

Step Action 1 Clear at least 3 m in every direction 2 Confirm that nobody is standing in front of the robot 3 Hold the button marked with a triangle. A short press is not enough 4 TTS: Entering dance mode. 5 Start a dance with R1+B 6 TTS: Please keep a safe distance. 7 When the dance ends, the robot switches to Running mode automatically

To stop a dance: double press START. This interrupts the running action.

Double START is not an emergency stop

A double press of START interrupts the action that is running. If the robot is walking with no action running, it goes into stepping in place instead of stopping. The emergency stop is L2+B; the normal stop is a single press of START. See Safety.

Torso brace

Dances do not run while the torso brace is fitted — the torso motors are deactivated. See Calibration.

docs.title: Squat, stand and seating
docs.text:
Squat/Stand is a toggle: the same combination L2+A works in both directions.

Situation Result Robot on the floor, L2+A pressed It squats → TTS Robot squatting. Please be careful. → Damp mode. — Damping engages automatically Robot on the gantry, L2+A pressed It squats, but Damping does not engage automatically. Switch to Damping manually

docs.title: Seating on a chair
docs.text:
1. Place a chair of suitable height behind the robot.
  2. Press L2+← for Seated Mode.
  3. Provide support from behind. The robot is not fully stable in this state.
  4. To stand up, press L2+↑ (Lock Stand → Ready), then R2+A.

Lock Stand holds the pose without balancing

In Ready mode the robot stands in a fixed pose with no active balancing, and it falls if pushed. This is an intermediate state — do not leave the robot in it unattended. Move to a working mode immediately.

docs.title: Shutdown
docs.text:
Step Action 1 Put the robot into Squat (L2+A), or suspend it on the gantry 2 Confirm the robot is in Damping mode. On the floor this engages automatically; on the gantry, hold L2+B to engage it manually 3 Press the battery button: one short press, then one long press

Damping before shutdown is mandatory

The robot must be in Damping before power-off. Zero Torque is not required. Power off only when the robot is suspended or seated — a standing robot with no support falls flat.

If the battery runs out during operation, the robot folds down on its own. No special action is required: pick it up and put it on charge.

During long idle periods, switch the robot into Damping periodically so that it does not stand under tension for weeks.

docs.title: Maintaining this manual

This manual documents firmware V1.0.4. When the robot is updated, verify the button layout against the legend printed on the remote and against the Unitree documentation for the new firmware version, then update the controls reference accordingly.

Report errors and submit corrections through the repository.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: Run through this page before every session with students.

docs.title: How to stop the robot
docs.text:
There is no physical emergency stop button on this delivery. Stopping the robot is a remote control action, and the correct action depends on the situation.

Situation Action Result The robot is walking somewhere you do not want it to go, and the situation is under control 1× START The robot enters Standing: it stops walking and remains standing A dance or gesture is running and must be cut short 2× START The running action is interrupted Emergency: unpredictable behaviour, risk to people L2+B Damping mode — the robot slowly sinks to the ground The remote control is dead or unresponsive Battery button Only after suspending the robot with its feet off the ground and at least 2 m of clear space around it. Otherwise it falls flat

Emergency stop

The emergency stop is L2+B

From the Unitree user manual: "Emergency Stop: When G1 appears in an unexpected state, press L2+B, G1 will enter damping mode and will slowly fall to the ground."

Teach this combination to students first, before anything else.

docs.title: Double START is not an emergency stop
docs.text:
A double press of START interrupts the action that is currently running. It stops a dance. It stops a gesture.

If the robot is simply walking and no action is running, there is nothing to interrupt: a double START puts the robot into Keep stepping — stepping in place. The robot will not run off, but it will not stop either, and the operator will believe they pressed stop. That false sense of safety is the danger.

  • Emergency stop: L2+B. The robot enters Damping and sinks to the floor.
  • Normal stop: one press of START. The robot stops walking and stays standing.

docs.title: Fall protection
docs.text: The robot has automatic fall protection: on detecting a fall, the motors switch to braking mode. The chassis is robust. This protection reduces damage — it does not replace correct stopping procedure.

docs.title: Safety checklist
docs.text: # Rule 1 Emergency stop is L2+B — the robot sinks slowly to the floor. Teach this to students first. The soft stop is a single press of START 2 Never activate Damping while the robot is standing unsupported. Torque is lost instantly and the robot falls. Squat it or suspend it first 3 Do not move the robot's joints by hand in Damping mode. This raises an error 4 Do not change wired network settings inside the robot. Recovering from this requires opening the back panel and reinstalling the operating system 5 Do not give a conversational live LLM direct control of the joints 6 Do not suspend the robot too high. It will not find the floor and will thrash its legs trying to reach it 7 Do not touch the LiDAR with your fingers. Clean it with microfibre only, without pressure 8 Do not mix up G1 and Go2 batteries or chargers 9 The remote control is highly sensitive. Move the sticks smoothly, in small increments 10 Walking backwards is unstable. The robot can fall. Walk backwards only with a spotter or on the gantry 11 Before Dance mode, clear the space and confirm nobody is standing in front of the robot 12 Gantry work takes two people — one steadies and moves the stand, one operates the remote 13 Remove or protect the head before working with a large group 14 Do not overtighten long bolts. Leverage strips the head 15 Starting from lying or squatting is allowed only on a flat, hard floor. With dexterous hands fitted, it is prohibited 16 A double press of START is not a stop. It interrupts a running action; a walking robot is put into stepping in place 17 Check the firmware version. Earlier revisions map these functions to L1 instead of L2 18 The robot powers itself off after 10 minutes of remote control inactivity. This is normal behaviour, not a fault 19 Do not flash the Jetson Orin NX module with third-party images 20 Keep your hands off the joints — hip and knee — when lifting the robot. They pinch 21 Power off only when the robot is suspended or seated, and in Damping. A standing robot with no support falls flat 22 The robot is neither waterproof nor dustproof. Dry, clean floor only, 0…40 °C 23 On tile, gloss and glass, reduce speed and avoid sharp movements. Do not operate on ice or on soft flooring 24 Top speed is 2 m/s. Keep people well clear 25 Do not calibrate on a schedule. Calibrate on symptoms only, after consulting your supplier

docs.title: What a violation costs
docs.text: At a competition, a robot fell during a sparring demonstration. Something in its back broke, there was a flash, and the robot never powered on again. The loss was total and irreversible.

docs.title: Practise independently
docs.text:
Work through this list before the next session. Start with the emergency stop and drill it until it is automatic.

  • Emergency stop L2+B — drill this first, to the point of reflex
  • Soft stop with a single press of START
  • Power-on and power-off to procedure, including the ≥2 s hold and the one-minute wait
  • The full startup chain: Zero Torque → L2+B → L2+↑ → R2+A
  • Posture transitions: L2+A squat, L2+← seated, L2+X lying and standing
  • Standing the robot up from the floor
  • Walking, turning, and switching speeds (2× L2 / 2× L1)
  • Drift compensation from the remote (R1 + arrows)
  • Interactive gestures (SELECT+A / +Y / +X)
  • Dance mode with the required clear space
  • Connecting the application in AP mode
  • Demo Teaching — record and replay your own gesture
  • Building a LiDAR map and a patrol route
  • Mounting the robot on the gantry and removing it

docs.title: Requires an instructor present
docs.text:
These are not to be attempted without an instructor:

  • Full calibration
  • Low-level joint control
  • Any work that involves opening the body

docs.title: Session structure for instructors
docs.text:
1. Run the pre-session checklist before students enter the room.
  2. Brief every new group on how to stop the robot before the robot is powered on.
  3. Keep the robot on the gantry for anything beyond basic walking and gestures.
  4. Clear 3 m in every direction before Dance mode, and confirm nobody stands in front of the robot.
  5. Shut down to procedure: squat or suspend, confirm Damping, then power off.

docs.title: Motion and stability
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action The robot drifts sideways when walking straight A small offset. This usually clears without calibration First: apply drift compensation from the remote — R1 + arrows inside Main Operation Control (R1+X / R1+Y). If that fails: run full body calibration After calibration the robot does not stand up by itself and has to be helped by hand The calibration did not complete correctly — not every joint reached its stop Repeat the calibration, driving every joint to its mechanical stop Flashing red in the application, Communication, joint over limit A joint is outside its permitted range. During calibration this means a brace was left on, most often on the foot Free and level the feet, then repeat the calibration from the start The torso does not move and dances do not run The torso brace is fitted, or the robot was not rebooted after removing it Remove the brace, then power the robot off and on The robot fell while being handled by hand Lock Stand was not run before the physical intervention Press L2+↑ before touching the robot The robot does not balance after Lock Stand Ready mode holds the pose without active balancing. This is normal behaviour Move to a working mode immediately (R2+A / R1+Y) and provide support The robot fell when started from lying Starting from lying or squatting is allowed only on a flat, hard floor, and is prohibited with dexterous hands fitted Move to a flat, hard floor, or lift the robot manually from the gantry

docs.title: Power and shutdown
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action The robot powered off by itself with no input Automatic power-off after 10 minutes of remote control inactivity Normal behaviour. Power it back on The robot fell while being powered off L2+B was pressed without support, or without holding the combination Squat the robot (L2+A) or suspend it first, and hold L2+B The robot fell flat during shutdown It was powered off standing, with no support Always power off suspended or seated, and in Damping The robot lay down on its own The battery ran out Normal behaviour. Pick it up and put it on charge

docs.title: Remote control
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action Buttons do not do what this manual describes Firmware older than V1.0.4 maps these functions to L1 Check the version in the application under About. On older firmware: Zero Torque L1+B, Damping L1+A, Lock Stand L1+↑ The remote behaves erratically, the sticks drift The joystick calibration has drifted, not the robot's F1+F3 → rotate both sticks fully around several times → F3 to save The remote does not bind The remote's code has not been entered Application → Settings → Remote Control Settings → enter the remote's code. The DL indicator lights when the link is established

docs.title: Gantry
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action The robot thrashes and cannot stand while suspended It is suspended too high and cannot find the floor Press L2+B (Damping). If that does not settle it, cut the power The robot does not move on the gantry The mount is fitted the wrong way round Refit the mount

docs.title: Application and connectivity
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action Android does not connect to the robot Priority mode switches the phone to mobile data Disable automatic switching or mobile data, or use a different phone The application does not connect over AP The access point name contains special characters or spaces, or the phone is too far away Rename the access point, move the phone closer, restart the robot and the application Firmware does not update The robot is in AP mode Switch to Wi-Fi mode and enable the OTA box The voice assistant does not respond No Wi-Fi, or the balance has not been topped up Check Wi-Fi and the account balance (from $15) The wrong map in Navigation A map from another robot, for example a Go2, is open Check which robot the map belongs to and recreate it if necessary The robot stopped along the route An obstacle was detected: There are obstacles in your way Normal behaviour. Clear the obstacle. The robot stops rather than routing around it

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Symptom Cause Action The SDK does not see the robot The devices are not on the same local network. There is no DHCP on the robot's network Confirm the laptop has a static address in 192.168.123.200–.250 with mask 255.255.255.0, and that 192.168.123.164 responds to ping The Jetson has no internet over Wi-Fi A static IP is set on the Wi-Fi hotspot Switch to Ethernet for development The robot feels tense in Zero Torque and jitters under SDK control The built-in motion control program always runs and sends speed-0 commands, which conflict with yours Enter Develop mode — L2+R2 while suspended and in Damping

docs.title: Anything else
docs.text: Run Log retrieval → Log upload in the application and report the issue to your supplier's support channel.

docs.title: Environment requirements
docs.text:
Parameter Requirement Clear space At least 2 metres to obstacles, uneven terrain, people and water Temperature 0…40 °C, good weather only Moisture and dust The robot is neither waterproof nor dustproof. Do not operate on a wet floor, in rain, on gravel, or in dust Floor Do not operate on ice or on soft flooring such as thick carpet. On tile, gloss and glass, reduce speed and avoid sharp movements Interference Do not operate near power lines or communication towers. If Wi-Fi is disrupted, switch off unnecessary signal sources Maximum speed Up to 2 m/s on a level floor Battery runtime ~2 hours of continuous operation

The 2-metre rule applies in every direction. For Dance mode, clear at least 3 metres.

docs.title: Pre-session checklist
docs.text:
1. Clear the space. At least 2 m in every direction. The floor must be level, dry and non-slip.

  2. Check the battery charge. Each unlit segment on the indicator is −25%. A battery gives about 2 hours of continuous operation, which does not cover a full teaching day — bring a second battery.

  3. Do not mix up batteries and chargers. The G1 battery is not compatible with the Go2 battery, and different G1 battery variants require different chargers.

    Danger

    Fitting the wrong battery or charger damages the equipment. Check the labels every time.

  4. Remove the protective film from the camera lens if it is still fitted, and check that the LiDAR dome is clean.

  5. Check the remote control. Confirm you have the G1 remote and not the Go2 remote — both live in the same case and are labelled. Compare the legend printed on the remote body against the controls reference.

  6. Check the firmware version in the mobile application under About. Older revisions map the mode functions to L1 instead of L2.

  7. Decide about the head. The head is the component most often damaged and most often modified. Before an active demonstration with students, remove it or suspend the robot on the gantry. Removal requires a Torx driver, not a hex key.

docs.title: Robotics Docs
docs.text:
В этом репозитории собрана документация по эксплуатации и разработке для робототехнических платформ Инженерной школы NewUU. Она написана для тех, кто действительно включает эти машины: преподавателей, ведущих лабораторные занятия, студентов, работающих по учебному плану, и разработчиков, чей код исполняется на роботе.

Каждая процедура здесь написана как процедура. Шаги пронумерованы, комбинации кнопок указаны точно, требования безопасности выделены отдельно. Выполняйте их в приведённом порядке.

Сайт доступен на английском и русском языках — переключайтесь селектором языка в шапке. Соседний значок переключает светлую и тёмную тему.

docs.title: Как стать контрибьютером
docs.text: Документация ведётся открыто. Если вы нашли ошибку или хотите добавить материал, откройте Issue или Pull Request.

docs.title: Правила создания Issue
docs.text:
1. Проверьте, что обращаетесь в нужный репозиторий.
  2. Если сообщаете об ошибке, убедитесь, что такого Issue ещё нет.
  3. Заполняйте заголовок и описание точно.
  4. Указывайте в заголовке один из флагов: [BUG], [PROPOSAL], [QUESTION].

docs.title: Правила создания Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Для небольших правок — опечатки, форматирование — предпочтительнее Pull Request.
  2. Опишите проблему и предлагаемое решение. При наличии укажите номер Issue.
  3. Прежде чем править форматирование, убедитесь, что это нужно.
  4. Придерживайтесь принятого в репозитории стиля Markdown.
  5. Английская версия — основная. Правку по существу вносите в обе языковые версии.

docs.title: Локальное развёртывание
docs.text:
Запуск документации в Docker-контейнере:

git clone https://github.com/NewUU-engineering/robotics-docs
cd robotics-docs
docker pull squidfunk/mkdocs-material
docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 -v ${PWD}:/docs squidfunk/mkdocs-material

Либо в виртуальном окружении Python:

python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocs-static-i18n[material]"
mkdocs serve

Сайт будет доступен по адресу http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Unitree G1 EDU — обзор
docs.text:
Это руководство по эксплуатации человекоподобного робота Unitree G1 EDU в поставке для Инженерной школы NewUU. Оно охватывает запуск, управление движением, калибровку, мобильное приложение, разработку на SDK, обслуживание и устранение неисправностей.

Сначала прочитайте раздел о безопасности

Аварийная остановка — L2+B. Физической кнопки аварийной остановки в этой поставке нет. Прочитайте Технику безопасности до подачи питания и проинструктируйте каждого нового оператора.

docs.title: Область применимости: прошивка
docs.text:
Руководство описывает прошивку V1.0.4. Проверьте версию прошивки в мобильном приложении в разделе About перед первым занятием.

Прошивка старше V1.0.4

В версиях до V1.0.4 вместо L2 используется L1: Zero Torque — L1+B, Damping — L1+A, Lock Stand — L1+↑. Все комбинации в этом руководстве приведены для V1.0.4.

docs.title: Старшинство источников
docs.text:
При расхождениях используйте источники в таком порядке:

  1. Легенда, напечатанная на самом пульте. Документация Unitree прямо направляет операторов к этой легенде как к основному источнику.
  2. Официальная документация Unitree для вашей версии прошивки.
  3. Это руководство.
  4. Поставщик — по всему, что не закрыто первыми тремя пунктами.

docs.title: Аппаратная конфигурация поставки
docs.text:
Узел Характеристика Модель Unitree G1, версия EDU (secondary development) Конфигурация U2 — 3 DoF в талии, 7 DoF в руках PC1 Материнская плата. Отвечает за локомоцию, стабилизацию и связь с пультом и приложением. Пользователю недоступна PC2 NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 100 TOPS, заводской образ Ubuntu 20.04. Полностью доступен для вашего кода PC1 ↔ PC2 Ethernet-кабель внутри робота Голова Камера глубины Intel RealSense D435i и LiDAR Livox MID-360 (360° по горизонтали, 59° по вертикали). Кабель LiDAR отсоединяется от платы; голова снимается ключом Torx, не шестигранником Порты 4× USB Type-C (один с DisplayPort), выход питания от батареи, pin-разъём для плат вроде Raspberry Pi, 2× RJ45 Батарея Индикатор с сегментами по 25%. Зарядное устройство 5 В. Не взаимозаменяема с батареей Go2 Уровень Установлен сзади на новых партиях. Используется для выравнивания робота при калибровке Кронштейн Стойка с лебёдкой и стропом. Робот может ходить в подвешенном состоянии Фиксаторы калибровки Механические стопоры на талию/торс, ноги и стопы, плюс фиксатор камеры. Комплект для Go2 — отдельный Инструмент в комплекте Т-образный вороток и плоскогубцы Пульты Два в кейсе — для G1 и для Go2, подписаны. Все комбинации напечатаны на пульте Кнопка аварийной остановки Не установлена. Дистрибьютор ставит её только на готовые решения для рынков EU и US

Различия партий

Партии поставки различаются. У новых экземпляров тише и стабильнее голова, громкость голоса примерно вдвое ниже, Wi-Fi на Jetson активирован из коробки, есть уровень для калибровки, другая ревизия платы Jetson и GPIO. Проверяйте конфигурацию своего экземпляра, а не полагайтесь на общее описание.

Сертификация

Роботы этой поставки не проходят европейскую сертификацию «как есть». Большую красную кнопку сверху дистрибьютор устанавливает только на готовые продукты для рынков EU и US.

docs.title: Порядок изучения
docs.text:
Новым операторам следует проходить руководство в таком порядке:

  1. Техника безопасности — как остановить робота и полный чек-лист.
  2. Справочник по управлению — карта режимов и полная таблица комбинаций.
  3. Подготовка рабочего места — требования к среде и чек-лист перед сессией.
  4. Штатные процедуры — от включения до выключения.
  5. Работа с кронштейном — безопасное рабочее положение для всего остального.

Разработчикам далее — Разработка. Преподавателям следует также прочитать Калибровку и Учебный план.

docs.title: Калибровка
docs.text: Калибровка — самая сложная процедура в этом руководстве. Прочитайте её целиком, прежде чем начинать.

docs.title: Когда калибровать
docs.text:
Не калибруйте планово

Из руководства пользователя Unitree: «G1 has been calibrated by default after leaving the factory. Do not recalibrate the joints for normal use! If any abnormal situation occurs with the G1, please consult Unitree's official technical support before determining whether joint recalibration is necessary.»

Калибруйте по симптому, а не по календарю. Плановая калибровка без причины — это регулярная возможность испортить исправную настройку.

Калибруйте, когда:

  • Робот часто падает при ходьбе, и перезагрузка не помогает.
  • Робот при движении прямо систематически уводит в сторону. Сначала попробуйте компенсацию смещения с пульта — R1 + стрелки.
  • Робот получил серьёзное падение или удар.

Согласуйте калибровку с поставщиком до начала работ. Путь в приложении: Settings → Data → Robot → Calibration.

docs.title: Три уровня калибровки
docs.text: Уровень Что делает Offset configuration Точечная подстройка смещения конкретного мотора числовым значением. Есть сброс IMU calibration / raw pitch Настройка баланса — наклон робота вперёд и назад, аналогично выставлению авиагоризонта Full body calibration Полная калибровка всех суставов: assisted (рекомендуется) или manual

docs.title: Подготовка
docs.text:
Шаг Действие 1 Переведите робота в Damping, затем полностью выключите питание 2 Снимите защитные крышки корпуса, если они есть в вашей версии. На новых версиях это не требуется 3 Установите механические фиксаторы на все суставы: талия/торс, ноги и стопы 4 Затяните винты фиксаторов. Затягивая несколько винтов на одной детали, делайте это равномерно, чтобы не перекосить деталь 5 Установите фиксатор камеры 6 Заблокируйте камеру через приложение 7 Выставьте робота ровно по встроенному уровню сзади или по индикатору в приложении 8 Подключите зарядный кабель. Калибровать при подключённом питании — нормально

Проверьте фиксатор на стопе

Фиксатор на стопе — наименее заметный из всех и тот, о котором забывают чаще всего. Без него калибровка проваливается.

Фиксатор торса деактивирует моторы торса

С установленным фиксатором торса робот ходит, но не танцует.

Не перетягивайте длинные болты

Рычаг срывает головку болта. Сломанные болты — повторяющаяся проблема, в том числе у инженеров самой Unitree.

docs.title: Full Body Calibration (assisted)
docs.text:
Шаг Действие Ожидаемый результат 1 Приложение → Full body calibration → Next Открывается экран Development mode 2 Выберите Assisted calibration, не Manual Робот начинает прогон 3 Робот сам прогоняет большую часть суставов — 4 Ноги: поднимите ногу вверх до упора, затем потяните её на себя до упора в другую сторону. Повторите на второй ноге Каждый сустав доведён до механического упора 5 Стопы: доверните стопу до упора. В финальном положении она должна быть строго ровной Этот шаг пропускают чаще всего 6 Руки: доведите до крайних положений плечо, локоть и предплечье, кисть Кисть вывернута до упора 7 Нажмите Calibration / Next и отойдите от робота — 8 Дождитесь статуса calibration successful — 9 Перезагрузите робота — 10 Снимите все фиксаторы — 11 Выключите и включите робота ещё раз Торс снова управляется

Шаг 11 обязателен

Без повторного цикла питания после снятия фиксаторов моторы торса остаются деактивированными.

Главное правило калибровки

Каждый сустав должен быть выведен в максимальный механический упор.

Режим assisted доводит не все суставы автоматически — часть придётся довести руками. Это всё равно значительно проще ручной калибровки.

docs.title: Критерии успеха
docs.text:
После перезагрузки перейдите в рабочий режим и убедитесь во всём перечисленном:

  • Робот самостоятельно встаёт в рабочую стойку, без помощи руками.
  • Он стоит по центру и ровно, не дрожит.
  • Ступни не цепляют пол.
  • При раскачивании вперёд и назад он не падает, а балансирует сам.
  • При ходьбе прямо он не уводит в сторону.
  • В приложении нет мигающего красного индикатора.

docs.title: Известный сценарий сбоя
docs.text:
Этап Что происходит Симптом После калибровки — мигающий красный индикатор и ошибка Communication, joint over limit Причина На стопе остался фиксатор. Режим assisted не смог довести этот сустав до упора, и у левой и правой ноги получились разные нулевые точки Решение Освободить и выровнять стопы, затем повторить полную калибровку с нуля Результат Калибровка проходит успешно, робот становится заметно стабильнее

Две гипотезы, которые обычно выдвигают при этом симптоме, неверны и отнимают время: неправильный порядок операций вокруг Lock Stand и низкий заряд батареи. Проверяйте в первую очередь фиксаторы, начиная со стоп.

docs.title: Справочник по управлению
docs.text: Все комбинации на этой странице приведены для прошивки V1.0.4. Проверьте версию прошивки в мобильном приложении в разделе About перед первым занятием.

docs.title: Комбинации кнопок
docs.text:
Действие Комбинация Питание вкл / выкл Кнопка на батарее: одно короткое нажатие, затем удержание ≥2 с Время загрузки ~1 минута до Zero Torque Zero Torque L2+Y Damping L2+B — из активного состояния комбинацию нужно удерживать, а не тапать Lock Stand → Ready L2+↑ Squat Switch L2+A (переключатель) Seated Mode L2+← Lying / Standing L2+X Debug Mode L2+R2 — входить, когда робот подвешен и находится в Damping Run Control R2+A Main Operation Control (талия 1 DoF) R1+X Main Operation Control (талия 3 DoF — наш робот) R1+Y — «Only Used For 3-DOF Waist Structure» Стоять ⇄ идти одно нажатие START Непрерывная ходьба двойное нажатие START — не рекомендуется Низкая / высокая скорость 2×L2 / 2×L1 (внутри R1+X, R1+Y) Медленный / быстрый бег R2+↓ / R2+↑ (внутри R2+A) Наклон вперёд / назад удержание START+↑ / START+↓ Компенсация смещения R1 + стрелки (внутри R1+X, R1+Y) Рукопожатие SELECT+A (удерживать SELECT, нажать A) Помахать рукой SELECT+Y Развернуться и помахать SELECT+X Аварийная остановка L2+B — робот медленно оседает на пол Подъём с пола L2+X Dance mode удержание кнопки «треугольник»; запуск танца — R1+B Калибровка пульта F1+F3 → покрутить оба стика до упора по кругу → F3 для сохранения

Значки на пульте

Треугольник рядом с кнопкой означает удержание. Звезда означает короткое нажатие.

docs.title: Режимы движения
docs.text:
Режим Вход Характер Main Operation Control R1+Y для нашего робота (талия 3 DoF); R1+X для конфигурации с талией 1 DoF Стабильнее, увереннее, заметно громче Run Control R2+A Быстрее, походка менее устойчивая

Unitree предписывает R1+Y для роботов с талией на 3 DoF: «Only Used For 3-DOF Waist Structure». У нашего экземпляра талия на 3 DoF, поэтому использовать следует R1+Y.

Непрерывная ходьба

Двойное нажатие START включает Continuous Walking, который Unitree помечает как не рекомендованный. Не путайте с одиночным нажатием START, которое останавливает ходьбу.

docs.title: Автоматическое выключение
docs.text: Робот выключается сам через 10 минут бездействия пульта.

docs.title: Архитектура
docs.text:
[Ноутбук разработчика]  192.168.123.200–250  (статика, DHCP НЕТ)

            │ 192.168.123.20                     [пульт ДУ]
